C08-M01-L01-F1.title: The tiered SOC: escalation up, feedback down
C08-M01-L01-F1.caption: Telemetry becomes alerts and cases; Tier 1 closes or escalates, higher tiers investigate, and lessons flow back to the detections.
C08-M01-L01-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom graph. Telemetry (endpoint, network, identity, cloud) feeds SIEM / EDR alerts (rules and models fire), which feed Case management (one record per case, owner, evidence), which feeds Tier 1: triage (validate, enrich, close or escalate). From Tier 1 one arrow goes to Closed with disposition (FP or benign true positive, documented) and another, labelled escalate, goes to Tier 2: investigation (scope, contain, coordinate IT). An arrow labelled escalate goes from Tier 2 to Tier 3: specialists (hunt, malware, forensics, detections). A dashed arrow labelled tuning and playbook feedback returns from Tier 3 to SIEM / EDR alerts. A SOC lead node (metrics, quality, stakeholders, CERT-In) has a dashed arrow labelled oversees to Case management.

C08-M01-L01-F1.note: Each tier receives fewer, harder cases than the one below it; knowledge flows back to improve the queue.

C08-M01-L01-F2.title: Classic tiers versus functional teams
C08-M01-L01-F2.caption: Two ways of building the same SOC funnel, compared on organisation, ownership, growth, repetitive work and cost.
C08-M01-L01-F2.alt: Two-column comparison. Classic tiered SOC: work organised by depth (T1, T2, T3); case changes hands at each escalation; clear entry role and career ladder; Tier 1 queue is repetitive, burnout risk; easy to staff and measure per tier. Versus Functional teams: work organised by function (detect, respond, hunt); one analyst owns a case end to end; mixed seniority within each team; repetitive triage automated (SOAR); needs strong automation and mentoring.

C08-M01-L01-F2.note: Most real SOCs blend the two: what matters is clear ownership, written criteria and a working feedback loop.
